dublinCore.title: FFT Size MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
FFT
Frequency Resolution
Signal Analysis
dublinCore.description: A sine-wave generator analysed with a selectable FFT size (512 to 8192 bins). The time-domain plot spans one window length and the spectrum draws one bar per bin, with read-outs of the bin width fs/N and the measured peak width at half height, so students see that a larger FFT gives narrower bins and peaks at the cost of a longer analysis window.
relation: Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

learningObjectives: Calculate the bin width (fs/N) and the window length (N/fs) for a given FFT size and sample rate
Predict how doubling the FFT size changes the bin width, the width of the spectral peak and the length of the analysis window
Explain the time-frequency trade-off: a larger FFT resolves frequency more finely only by analysing a longer stretch of signal, because the bin width times the window length equals 1
Explain why the strongest bin can differ from the true tone frequency by up to half a bin width
Determine which FFT sizes can separate two tones a given distance apart, using the measured peak width
prerequisites: Sine waves: frequency, period and amplitude

misconceptions.misconception: A bigger FFT is always better
misconceptions.correction: A larger FFT gives narrower peaks only by analysing a longer stretch of signal, so it blurs changes in time and costs more computation
misconceptions.evidence: At 8192 bins each spectrum depends on 341 ms of signal; a quick amplitude dip appears as a gap travelling across the whole time window

misconceptions.misconception: The FFT reports the exact frequency of the tone
misconceptions.correction: The FFT measures only at the bin frequencies k fs/N, so the strongest bin can be off by up to half a bin
misconceptions.evidence: At 512 bins and 48 kHz a 440 Hz tone appears at 421.9 Hz

misconceptions.misconception: The peak of a pure tone should be a single thin line
misconceptions.correction: A finite window spreads a pure tone over several bins (about 2.4 bins at half height for the Blackman window); the peak narrows in hertz as N grows
misconceptions.evidence: The measured half-height width falls from 113.8 Hz at 512 bins to 6.9 Hz at 8192 bins (48 kHz), always about 2.4 bins

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A sine-wave generator analysed by an FFT whose size you choose with radio buttons from 512 to 8192 bins. The top plot shows a stretch of the waveform one analysis window long; the bottom plot shows the magnitude spectrum from 0 to 2100 Hz as one bar per frequency bin. Larger FFT sizes give narrower bins, a narrower peak and a longer analysis window.

controls.label: Frequency
controls.description: Sets the frequency of the sine wave

controls.label: Amplitude
controls.description: Sets the peak amplitude of the sine wave (the speaker plays it at half this level)

controls.label: Start / Pause
controls.description: Starts audio on the first click, then toggles the tone and the live analysis on and off

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns the sliders to 440 Hz and amplitude 0.5 (the FFT size is kept)

controls.label: FFT Size (bins)
controls.description: Chooses the number of frequency bins between 0 Hz and fs/2; each spectrum uses N = 2 x size samples, so the bin width is fs/N

visualElements.description: Time-domain plot (green): a stretch of the waveform one analysis window long (N samples), with a millisecond axis; short windows are triggered on a rising zero crossing
Frequency-domain plot (purple): one bar per FFT bin from 0 to 2100 Hz, with a gold marker on the strongest bin and a gold bracket across the peak at half height
Status indicator (RUNNING / PAUSED), strongest-bin frequency and magnitude, frequency resolution fs/N and measured peak width at half height

model.description: An oscillator produces x(t) = A sin(2 pi f t). The browser's analyser (via p5.sound 0.4.1) applies a Blackman window to the most recent N = 2 x size samples and computes an N-point FFT; the sketch plots each bin's magnitude, normalised so that an amplitude-1 sine centred on a bin reaches 1, and measures the peak width at half height by linear interpolation between bins.
equations: x(t) = A sin(2 pi f t)
algorithms: Half-height peak width by linear interpolation
Rising zero-crossing trigger for short time windows
limitations: The strongest-bin read-out can differ from the slider frequency by up to half a bin
The time plot shows a stretch of signal one window long that lags the spectrum slightly, because the waveform buffer is read from the older part of the analyser's history
A tone between two bins reads up to about 12% low because of the Blackman window

instructionalStrategies: Predict-then-verify the bin width and peak width before each size change
Worksheet table of N, T, bin width and peak width for every FFT size
Observing a quick amplitude dip with long and short windows to discuss the time-frequency trade-off
extensions: Add a second oscillator to test which FFT sizes separate two close tones
Compare with a short-time Fourier transform spectrogram and its window-length setting
